transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO), Olivia (Head of ML), Ravi (DevOps)

Summary: quick discovery focused on perf targets (p95), concurrency and bench template, clarify hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Diego on the eng side. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Samir: good thanks, quick note we're on a bit of a timebox, 45-60 minutes is ideal. we're trying to validate whether Redwood Hosted can meet our latency p95 and if not what Dedicated/Private path looks like.
[00:25] Diego: totally, we'll try to cover measurement plan and what the POC looks like. quick q to start — what's your main SLOs today?
[00:33] Olivia: for chat we need p95 end-to-end under ~300ms for short assist responses (like 16-64 tokens). for longer generation we care more about throughput but still want predictable tail — p95 under 800ms for 256 token completions. concurrency wise we expect bursts up to 150 concurrent users hitting chat, steady-state 40-60.
[00:56] Ravi: and we need streaming first-byte latency good for UX — ideally <150ms p95 on the first token.
[01:10] Maya: okay that's helpful. when you say end-to-end, do you include network + pre/post processing on your side?
[01:18] Olivia: yes includes our edge services and some light prompt engineering, so we have ~20-40ms of client side work. the 300ms is the full user-perceived p95.
[01:30] Diego: noted. couple of clarifying Qs — what models are you running today and are you open to quantized variants?
[01:38] Samir: we run a fine-tuned open-arch model (a 13B-ish) on-prem now. we can try quantized versions, but quality regressions are a concern. also security: SOC2, SSO, KMS for keys.
[01:52] Maya: we support SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integrations for Private. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:00] Diego: on perf side: for Hosted we have curated model profiles — the tradeoffs are lower friction vs slightly higher variance under noisy multi-tenant load. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable p95 and configured batch windows; Private is similar but you manage network.
[02:20] Olivia: can you explain how KV cache warm/cold affects p95 for convo-style streaming?
[02:27] Diego: yeah, so KV cache warm means the model doesn't need to re-encode prior tokens; first byte is faster. cold-cache scenarios add overhead on the first request or after long idle periods. for convo workloads with sticky sessions we typically see much lower p95. we'll capture warm/cold in the benchmark template.
[02:44] Samir: how do you measure token/sec in your benchmarks? we've got a few internal metrics — tokens/sec per GPU, and end-to-end tokens/sec as seen from our app.
[02:56] Diego: our benchmark template includes both microbenchmarks (tokens/sec raw on model instance) and end-to-end synthetic workload tests with network overhead. typical numbers we quote: for 13B quantized on A100-class or equivalent you might see 300-800 tokens/sec depending on batch/seq length. but real numbers depend on prompt length, streaming chunk size, batch policy.
[03:20] Olivia: what's your streaming chunking policy? does Redwood support smaller first-chunk sizes to improve first-byte latency?
[03:28] Diego: yes we support configurable chunk sizes and we can prioritize early tokens — there's a tradeoff with throughput because smaller chunks reduce batching efficiency. in Dedicated you can tune batching windows to hit your 1) p95 for first byte and 2) aggregate tokens/sec.
[03:45] Ravi: what about concurrency headroom — if we need 150 concurrent users with average 2 r/s each, how do you size Dedicated?
[03:54] Diego: we'd ask for more specifics (avg tokens per request, seq lengths). rough example: if avg request is 64 tokens and you want 150 concurrent with target 400 tokens/sec aggregate, we might size a pool of N GPUs with autoscale/burst — the benchmark will provide exact numbers. for initial POC we'll run a synthetic traffic replay from your traces you mentioned.
[04:18] Olivia: yes we'll share two weeks of traces — mostly short chat, some longer summarization flows.
[04:25] Maya: perfect — Olivia, if you can drop those to the shared drive we'll pick them up.
[04:30] Samir: curious on tail behavior — how does your routing handle noisy neighbors on Hosted? do you have fallback to cheaper models?
[04:40] Diego: we have smart routing by policy — you can route by latency, cost, region; and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constrained. Hosted is multi-tenant but we pro-actively isolate noisy tenants with scheduling. Dedicated avoids that entirely.
[04:56] Maya: any regulatory or data residency constraints we should know?
[05:00] Ravi: EU customer data must not leave EU regions; we expect Private/VPC for that.
[05:06] Maya: noted, for Private we can keep control plane local. we'll include VPC network checklist.
[05:12] Diego: let's talk concrete P95 numbers — you asked for ~300ms p95 on short replies. on Hosted with a standard shared pool we can often hit 200-400ms p95 for 13B quantized on average; p95 variance increases with concurrency. Dedicated will get you more consistent p95 ~150-300ms depending on instance class and batch settings.
[05:36] Olivia: can you run a quick example — what drivers change the p95? like batch window, chunk size, quantization?
[05:44] Diego: sure — batch window bigger increases throughput but can add queuing latency up to the window length; quantization reduces per-token compute time but might add decoding overhead and small quality hit; KV cache warm reduces end-to-end for multi-turn; network and pre/post processing add fixed overhead. we'll instrument all of these in the POC.
[06:05] Maya: regarding cost, customers often trade a small increase in infra for Dedicated to get stable p95; is that something you're open to?
[06:14] Samir: yes but we need to justify cost with predictable unit economics — i.e., cost per 1M tokens at our observed distribution.
[06:22] Diego: we'll produce token-level cost breakdowns and a recommended autoscale policy that tries to minimize spend while keeping your p95 SLO.
[06:31] Olivia: about benchmarking — we want both synthetic runs and replay of our production traces. do you support trace replay?
[06:38] Diego: yes we'll replay traces in the POC. we'll need the trace format — we'll share the template.
[06:43] Ravi: any gotchas for private/on-prem in terms of kernel support or particular GPU drivers?
[06:49] Diego: we support a set of validated drivers and kernels. on-prem installs need matching CUDA/cuDNN versions; we'll provide a compatibility matrix. sometimes microcode variance can affect perf by single-digit percent.
[07:05] Samir: let's walk through the POC plan high level.
[07:09] Diego: proposed POC: 1) Redwood sends benchmark template + sample scripts; 2) Aurora provides traces and target SLOs; 3) Redwood runs synthetic microbenchmarks (tokens/sec, cold/warm cache), and 2 full replays (one hosted, one dedicated) and returns p95/throughput/cost report; 4) adjust config and rerun. aim for 2 weeks.
[07:34] Olivia: timeline works. who owns the Hosted vs Dedicated sizing?
[07:38] Diego: SE (me) will size initial Dedicated pool based on traces; we'll propose autoscale settings and burst policy. final size validated by POC.
[07:47] Maya: any questions on compliance?
[07:50] Olivia: SSO SAML and KMS for keys; audit logs for model inputs for 90 days.
[07:57] Maya: we support all that, will send SOC2 report + audit log options.
[08:03] Samir: what's the typical first-byte streaming p95 you achieve on production workloads?
[08:10] Diego: for warm-cache convo flows we commonly see first-byte p95 ~80-150ms on Dedicated; Hosted is typically 100-200ms but more variance. again depends on instance class and model size.
[08:24] Olivia: how do you handle fallback when Dedicated is saturated?
[08:29] Diego: we can route overflow to a lower-cost Dedicated tier or to Hosted with a graceful degradation policy; you can configure canary failover.
[08:38] Ravi: are there limits around concurrent streaming connections per instance?
[08:42] Diego: there's OS/socket and runtime limits but we manage connection pools and recommend a fronting layer that multiplexes. we'll include recommended Nginx/nginx-like settings in the network checklist.
[08:55] Maya: ok let's capture concrete metrics we need from you: Olivia/Samir, please share trace samples, target SLOs per flow (chat short, chat long, summarization), and peak concurrency windows.
[09:08] Olivia: will do.
[09:11] Samir: question about token accounting — do you measure billing tokens as model input+output or just output?
[09:17] Maya: Redwood billing counts both input and output tokens; we'll provide breakdowns in the cost report.
[09:24] Diego: quick note about token/sec bench: we measure raw model tokens/sec at the runtime boundary and separately end-to-end including network; both will be in the report with the scripts we run.
[09:34] Olivia: on quantization — if we see a small quality delta, can we pin to non-quantized in Dedicated?
[09:40] Diego: yes you can pin to a full-precision variant for Dedicated, and set fallbacks. but cost will be higher.
[09:48] Maya: next steps recap — we'll send pricing + POC template, Diego will propose times for the 2-hr benchmark window, and customer to share traces and SLOs.
[09:58] Olivia: sounds good.
[10:01] Samir: one last item — can you include a sample per-route dashboard so we can see how you'd show p95 and token costs?
[10:08] Maya: yes we'll attach screenshots of Redwood Console and a sample per-route breakdown in the follow-up.
[10:15] Diego: any final technical clarifications?
[10:18] Ravi: none from me.
[10:20] Maya: great thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack.
[10:24] Samir: thanks everyone.
